title: Schlessinger hull criterion and rigidity for deformation groupoids
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathrm{Art}_k$ be the category of commutative Artinian local $k$-algebras with specified residue field $k$ and local $k$-homomorphisms inducing its identity. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize. Let $\mathcal D$ be a pseudofunctor from $\mathrm{Art}_k$ to groupoids (categories whose arrows are invertible), with $\mathcal D(k)$ equivalent to the one-object one-arrow category. Assume that for every $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ with $A_2\to A$ surjective, restriction induces an equivalence
$$\mathcal D(A_1\times_A A_2)\simeq\mathcal D(A_1)\times_{\mathcal D(A)}\mathcal D(A_2).$$
The groupoid on the right has triples $(x_1,x_2,\alpha:x_1|_A\cong x_2|_A)$ and pairs of arrows commuting with $\alpha$. Put $F(A)=\pi_0\mathcal D(A)$, the set of isomorphism classes. Its tangent space $T=F(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ has the deformation vector operations: scalar multiplication is induced by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$; addition is obtained by the displayed equivalence over $k$, followed by the homomorphism $k\oplus(k\oplus k)\to k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ sending $(a,(b,c))$ to $a+(b+c)\epsilon$. Suppose $\dim_kT<\infty$. There exist a complete Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and a natural map $\eta:h_B\to F$, where $h_B(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k,\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{cont}}(B,A)$ and continuity uses maximal-ideal-adic topologies, such that
$$h_B(A')\longrightarrow h_B(A)\times_{F(A)}F(A')$$
is surjective for every surjection $A'\to A$, and $\eta:T h_B\to T$ is a $k$-linear isomorphism. Such a map is called a hull. Let $x_\epsilon$ be the pullback to $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ of an object over $k$, and let $\operatorname{Inf}(\mathcal D)$ be its automorphism group. If $\operatorname{Inf}(\mathcal D)$ is trivial, every hull $h_B\to F$ is a natural isomorphism.

proof.text: Take $R=k$ in the test-category definition. The hypothesis on $\mathcal D$ is exactly predeformation plus (RS). The tangent-tensor lemma identifies $F(k[W])$ with $T\otimes_k W$, naturally in finite-dimensional $W$. Choose a basis $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_d$ of $T$. Apply the completed-polynomial lemma with $P=k[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$, augmentation $X_i\mapsto0$, completion $S$ and maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Put $J_1=\mathfrak m$, $J_2=\mathfrak m^2$. Its Artinian-map bijection identifies $S/J_2=k[k^d]$: maps to any test algebra killing products of the $X_i$ are exactly maps from this square-zero algebra. Choose $\xi_1\in\mathcal D(k)$ and $\xi_2\in\mathcal D(S/J_2)$ representing $\sum_i\theta_i\otimes e_i$, with its unique restriction isomorphism to $\xi_1$. A local map $S\to k[\epsilon]$ is uniquely specified by $X_i\mapsto a_i\epsilon$, and sends this class to $\sum_i a_i\theta_i$. This is a linear bijection, including $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 06IW (lemma-versal-object-existence), Steps 1--2; classical-case refinement in Tag 06IX (theorem-miniversal-object-existence).

proof.text: Suppose $n\geq2$, $\mathfrak m^n\subseteq J_n\subseteq J_{n-1}$ and compatible objects through $\xi_n\in\mathcal D(S/J_n)$ have been chosen. The ring $S/(\mathfrak mJ_n)$ is Artinian by the completed-polynomial lemma, since $\mathfrak m^{n+1}\subseteq\mathfrak mJ_n$. The kernel of its surjection to $S/J_n$ is killed by its maximal ideal. Apply the minimal-liftable-ideal lemma to $\xi_n$. Taking inverse images in $S$ gives $\mathfrak mJ_n\subseteq J_{n+1}\subseteq J_n$ and an object $\xi_{n+1}$ restricting isomorphically to $\xi_n$. Retain that isomorphism. This preserves $\mathfrak m^{n+1}\subseteq J_{n+1}$. Its crucial leastness property is: if $\mathfrak mJ_n\subseteq K\subseteq J_n$ and $\xi_n$ lifts to $S/K$, then $J_{n+1}\subseteq K$. Starting with step 1 constructs the entire compatible system.

Put $J=\bigcap_{n\geq1}J_n$ and $B=S/J$. The complete-local-quotient lemma makes $B$ Noetherian complete local with residue field $k$. The descending-ideal lemma applies to $\mathfrak m^n\subseteq J_n$ and makes $(J_n/J)$ cofinal with the maximal-ideal powers of $B$. The formal-filtration comparison gives a formal object $\xi$ on $B$, whose evaluation over $S/J_n$ is compatibly $\xi_n$. In particular it defines a natural transformation $\eta:h_B\to F$ by taking isomorphism classes of evaluations. For any local map $B\to A$, nilpotence of $\mathfrak m_A$ ensures that some maximal-ideal power of $B$ maps to zero; hence it is continuous and the evaluation is defined. Since $J\subseteq J_2=\mathfrak m^2$, every tangent map of $S$ kills $J$. Thus tangent maps of $B$ and $S$ coincide, and the evaluation clause identifies their tangent map to $T$ with the linear bijection of step 1.

source.place: Tag 06IW (lemma-versal-object-existence), passage to the limit; classical-case tangent refinement in Tag 06IX.

proof.text: To test the ring-lifting condition for versality, let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a small extension, $a:B\to A$ a local $k$-map and $y\in\mathcal D(A')$ with a specified comparison $y|_A\cong\xi_a$. Nilpotence and cofinality in step 3 let $a$ factor through $S/J_n\to A$ for some $n\geq2$. The comparison identifies $\xi_a$ with the image of $\xi_n$. The test-algebra lemma gives $E=(S/J_n)\times_A A'$ and a small extension $p:E\twoheadrightarrow S/J_n$. By (RS), the triple $(\xi_n,y,\text{comparison})$ lifts to an object in $\mathcal D(E)$ restricting to $\xi_n$. If $p$ has a section, $B\to S/J_n\to E\to A'$ is already the required ring lift of $a$. Otherwise $p$ is essential by the small-extension-essential lemma.

source.place: Tag 06IW (lemma-versal-object-existence), versality argument through the section case.

proof.text: In the nonsplit case, lift $S\to S/J_n\to A$ to $h:S\to A'$ by the completed-polynomial lemma. Then $g:S\to E$, $s\mapsto(s\bmod J_n,h(s))$, is local, residue-preserving, and surjective by the complete-source clause of essentiality. For $K=\ker(g)$ we have $K\subseteq J_n$. Moreover $g(J_n)\subseteq\ker(p)$, which is killed by the maximal ideal of $E$; locality gives $\mathfrak mJ_n\subseteq K$. The object over $E=S/K$ supplied in step 4 lifts $\xi_n$, so the leastness in step 2 gives $J_{n+1}\subseteq K$. Therefore $g$ factors through $S/J_{n+1}$; precompose its projection to $A'$ with $B\to S/J_{n+1}$ to lift $a$. This checks the underlying-ring condition of the tangent-ring-lift criterion. Step 3 gives its tangent surjectivity; that criterion supplies the comparison isomorphism extending the prescribed one and gives versality for all Artinian surjections. Passing to isomorphism classes proves the asserted surjectivity of $h_B(A')\to h_B(A)\times_{F(A)}F(A')$, so together with step 3 this is a hull.

source.place: Tags 06IW (lemma-versal-object-existence), final argument, and 06IU (lemma-versal-criterion); passing to classes as in 06IZ (remark-compose-minimal-into-iso-classes).

proof.text: Assume now $\operatorname{Inf}(\mathcal D)=0$. For any $x\in\mathcal D(A)$ factor $A\twoheadrightarrow k$ into small extensions by the test-algebra lemma. At each stage the automorphism-kernel lemma says the kernel of automorphism reduction is a torsor under $0\otimes_k I=0$, hence has a single element, necessarily the identity. Thus each reduction map on automorphism groups is injective. Their composite maps to the trivial automorphism group over $k$, so $\operatorname{Aut}(x)=1$. Any two arrows between fixed objects therefore agree, since their quotient is an automorphism. For $P=A_1\times_A A_2$, compatible isomorphism classes in $F(A_1)\times_{F(A)}F(A_2)$ admit an isomorphism over $A$ by the meaning of equality of classes. This isomorphism is unique. Triples with the same component classes are uniquely isomorphic, since their component arrows commute over $A$ by uniqueness. The (RS) equivalence consequently gives a bijection $F(P)\cong F(A_1)\times_{F(A)}F(A_2)$. Also $F(k)$ is a singleton. Thus $F$ satisfies the set-valued hypotheses of the lift-torsor lemma.

Let $\rho:h_C\to F$ be any hull. Local maps from $C$ to Artinian targets are continuous: a local map sends a high maximal-ideal power to zero, by nilpotence of the target maximal ideal. Thus compatible maps to $A_1,A_2$ define a unique local continuous map to their ring fibre product, coordinatewise. Hence $h_C$ preserves these fibre products and $h_C(k)$ is a singleton. Regard $h_C$ and $F$ as discrete groupoid-valued pseudofunctors. Their marked lift classes are exactly their ordinary set fibres, since the only isomorphisms are identities. Apply the marked-lift-torsor lemma to them and $\rho$. Its tangent map is an isomorphism by the definition of a hull. For a small extension $p:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, assume $\rho_A$ is bijective. Given $z\in F(A')$, choose the unique $u\in h_C(A)$ with $\rho_A(u)=F(p)(z)$. Hull smoothness supplies a lift $u'\in h_C(A')$ mapping to $z$, proving surjectivity. If two lifts have the same image, their restrictions agree by injectivity over $A$. The nonempty fibres over that restriction and its image are torsors by the lemma, and the map is equivariant for the isomorphism $T h_C\otimes_k I\to T F\otimes_k I$. If the lifts differ by $v$, their common image forces $(d\rho\otimes1)(v)=0$, so $v=0$ and the lifts agree. This proves injectivity. Start with $A=k$, where both sets are singletons, and induct along a factorization of any $A\twoheadrightarrow k$ into small extensions. Every $\rho_A$ is bijective; the inverses are natural by naturality of $\rho$, proving the last clause for every hull.

Steps 1-5 follow 06IW with Lambda=R=k. Here J_2=m^2, so the tangent map is the bijection of the classical 06IX case: maps X_i->a_i eps give sum a_i theta_i by the 1-tensor-lambda naturality of rs-tangent-tensor. In the induction, S/mJ_n is Artinian because m^{n+1} is contained in mJ_n, which is contained in m, and the least liftable ideal is applied correctly. In the limit, J is contained in m^2 and is proper; complete-local-quotient, 06SE cofinality and 06H6 evaluation then apply. For versality, E=S/J_n x_A A' is a small extension; the section case gives the lift, otherwise the complete-source essential clause makes g surjective. K=ker g lies in J_n and contains mJ_n, so leastness gives J_{n+1} in K. The tangent-ring-lift criterion then gives versality, and passing to iso classes gives the hull. Step 6 (Inf=0): the kernel node on each small extension gives injective reductions, so Aut(x)=1, and RS then gives the set-valued fibre-product bijection. Step 7 is the 06JL induction through the marked-lift-torsor node (Q49, on base) on discrete groupoids, for every hull. The new node matches 06JX+06JY: since D(k) is trivial, Inf_{x0}=Aut(x_eps). I tested it on I=0 and on the one-object D with Aut=1+m_A, where the kernel 1+I is k tensor I; it is not elementary and not a clause of the parent.
